title: The approved Product Contract and the PRD dossier are readable on the goal
description:
SPIDR child 2 of task-e7a20a498ed0436380e5aca23cb81607 (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-05). Dependency-free LEAF; parallel with child 1.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: two daemon reads that are SERVED but have no screen, given one each. (a) The approved Product Contract dossier on the opened goal from `/product-contract/gate-1/read`: personas/journeys, requirements, criteria WITH their coverage state, assumptions, unresolved decisions, versions. (b) The document dossier on the PRD panel from `/documents/dossier/read`.

MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-20a6d1eb - both reads exist DAEMON-SIDE, so this row is browser work plus decoders, not new routes:
- `apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener-read-dispatch.ts` imports `PRODUCT_CONTRACT_GATE_1_READ_PATH` with `handleProductContractGate1ReadRequest` (:11-12) and `DOCUMENT_DOSSIER_PATH` with `handleDocumentDossierReadRequest` (:3). Both are wired.
- `/documents/dossier/read` is ALREADY in the browser's proxy roster (apps/control-room/src/live/dev-proxy-paths.ts:16); `/product-contract/gate-1/read` is NOT - so that one needs its proxy pin as well as its decoder.
- `grep -rn 'gate-1/read' apps/control-room/src` returns nothing outside the proxy list, so neither read is consumed by a screen today. That is the gap, and it is real.

THE DECODER DISCIPLINE: every live read client in apps/control-room/src/live/ decodes with an EXACT-KEY record check that REFUSES a response whose key set differs, rather than silently defaulting - a stale daemon is detected, not papered over. Follow that shape (live-sessions.ts is a compact example); a decoder that tolerates extra keys is how a shape change ships unnoticed.

CRITERIA COVERAGE STATE is the load-bearing column: the contract dossier shows each criterion WITH whether it is covered, which is what makes the screen worth opening rather than a formatted dump of the contract.
definitionOfDone: The opened goal shows the approved Product Contract dossier from `/product-contract/gate-1/read`: the approved revision id, the requirements count, and every criterion WITH its coverage state. Assert against a REAL daemon frame that a named criterion's coverage state reaches the row - a dossier that lists criteria without coverage is a formatted dump, not a dossier.
The PRD panel shows the document dossier from `/documents/dossier/read`.

Both reads have an EXACT-KEY decoder that REFUSES an unexpected key set rather than defaulting, with a test for each: a real frame decodes; a frame with an extra key is refused; a frame missing a key is refused. `/product-contract/gate-1/read` also gains its proxy pin in dev-proxy-paths.ts (`/documents/dossier/read` is already there at :16 - do not duplicate it).

Every digest mirror and roster the new decoders touch is updated together: packages generated-coverage.test.ts, apps/control-room/src/data/data-adapter.test.ts and v2/goals/approve-plan.test.tsx are the ones the parent row names - verify each by running it, and if one does not in fact pin this surface, say so in the step note rather than editing it for symmetry.
Refusals render VERBATIM with their codes on both screens - a goal whose contract read refuses must say so, not render an empty dossier that reads as 'no requirements'.

This row adds NO daemon route: `git diff --stat` shows no file under apps/daemon/src. Gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` (the packages digest mirrors are touched, so the root lane is real evidence here).
taskRails: BROWSER-ONLY. Both reads are already served; this row writes decoders and screens. A daemon change means the read is not what it claims - stop and report rather than editing it.
EXACT-KEY DECODERS, matching every sibling in apps/control-room/src/live/. A tolerant decoder defeats the mechanism that detects a stale daemon.

AN EMPTY DOSSIER IS NEVER RENDERED AS EMPTINESS. A refusal renders its code; absence of data renders words saying so. The difference matters because an operator reads an empty requirements list as 'the contract has none'.
ASCII-only sources and apostrophe-free JSX text (scheduler package-boundary scan); check any new testid namespace is free; keep every production file under 250 lines.

implementationPlan.description: READ THE CORRECTION, THEN RE-MEASURE, NO EDITS. comment-9dc329557e594da39b32226525d1c66d on this row corrects its own description: only ONE of the two reads is unconsumed. Verify: (a) `/documents/dossier/read` ALREADY has a decoder (`apps/control-room/src/live/live-document-dossier.ts`, exporting `createLiveDocumentDossierFeed`), a component (`apps/control-room/src/preview/document-dossier.tsx` with document-dossier-state.ts), a test, and a proxy pin (dev-proxy-paths.ts:16) — but is consumed only by the LEGACY surface (`live-app.tsx:6-20`, reached via development-legacy-root.tsx:3 and shell-mode-view.tsx:5), while `main.tsx:12` mounts v2's `CordumApp`. `grep -rn 'document-dossier|DocumentDossier' apps/control-room/src/v2` = ZERO. (b) `/product-contract/gate-1/read` has NO browser consumer and NO proxy pin; its daemon side is real (product-contract-gate-1-read.ts:27 path, :60 `ProductContractGate1View` with `outcome: "GATE"`, :70 refusal, :80 port). (c) Record the pre-change `Test Files N passed` for `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`.

THE GATE-1 DECODER — the genuinely new one. Add a live read client for `/product-contract/gate-1/read` beside its siblings in apps/control-room/src/live/, following their EXACT-KEY discipline: decode the response with an exact-key record check that REFUSES a key set that differs rather than defaulting (live-sessions.ts is the compact example), and decode the two shapes the daemon actually serves — `{outcome: "GATE", gate: ...}` (product-contract-gate-1-read.ts:113) and the refusal `{code, layer, outcome: "REFUSED"}` (:70-73, :87). Add its pin to dev-proxy-paths.ts (the sorted list at :6-37); `/documents/dossier/read` is ALREADY there at :16 — do not duplicate it. Test three ways: a real frame decodes; a frame with an EXTRA key is refused; a frame MISSING a key is refused. A tolerant decoder defeats the mechanism that detects a stale daemon.

THE CONTRACT DOSSIER ON THE GOAL. Render the approved revision id, the requirements count, and EVERY CRITERION WITH ITS COVERAGE STATE, plus personas/journeys, assumptions, unresolved decisions and versions. THE COVERAGE COLUMN IS THE LOAD-BEARING ONE: a list of criteria without coverage is a formatted dump of the contract, and the operator can already read the contract — what they cannot see anywhere else is which criteria are actually covered. Assert against a REAL daemon frame that a NAMED criterion's coverage state reaches the rendered row, not merely that a table rendered. Keep the screen in its own module under apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/ and under 250 lines.

THE PRD DOSSIER IN v2 — BY REUSE, NOT BY REBUILD. Consume the EXISTING `createLiveDocumentDossierFeed` and the existing `preview/document-dossier.tsx` component from the v2 PRD panel. DO NOT write a second decoder or a second component for a read the browser already decodes and renders — a parallel implementation is the duplication this board keeps paying for. FIRST MEASURE whether that component renders acceptably inside the v2 shell: if it needs a v2-native presentation, say so in a step note and adapt the PRESENTATION while still consuming the existing FEED and state module. Assert the PRD dossier renders in v2 against a real frame, and that the legacy surface still renders it unchanged (its count line unchanged from step 1).

REFUSALS RENDER, ABSENCE IS WORDS. Both surfaces render a refusal VERBATIM with its code. And the distinction that matters: a goal whose contract read REFUSES must say so — it must NOT render an empty dossier, because an empty requirements list reads to an operator as 'this contract has no requirements', which is a different and false claim. Assert three states per surface: a real frame renders; a refusal renders its code; genuinely-absent data renders words saying it is absent. Also assert that a refusal on ONE of the two reads does not blank the OTHER.

DIGEST MIRRORS, DRILL, GATES. (a) The row's DoD 4 names three files as digest mirrors to update together — packages generated-coverage.test.ts, apps/control-room/src/data/data-adapter.test.ts and v2/goals/approve-plan.test.tsx. VERIFY EACH BY RUNNING IT rather than editing for symmetry: if one does not in fact pin this surface, say so in the step note and leave it alone. An edit made to satisfy a list rather than a failure is how a test stops meaning what its name says. (b) DRILL (global rail 1): make the new gate-1 decoder tolerant of an extra key — the step-2 refusal arm must go RED; restore. The new files are UNTRACKED until committed and `git diff` is blind to untracked paths, so prove that restore by SHA256 against an out-of-tree backup in %TEMP% suffixed by worker id, in a call SEPARATE from the restore (global rail 13). (c) SCOPE PROOF: `git diff --stat` shows NO file under apps/daemon/src — both reads are already served. (d) ASCII-only sources and apostrophe-free JSX text (scheduler package-boundary scan); check the testid namespace is free. (e) GATES with count lines quoted (global rail 8): `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`, and `pnpm test` — real evidence here only if a packages/ digest mirror was actually touched; say which. Named verification command: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`.

And `grep -rn "document-dossier|DocumentDossier" apps/control-room/src/v2` returns ZERO: v2 does not consume it.

CONSEQUENCE FOR DoD 3 ("Both reads have an EXACT-KEY decoder ... with a test for each"): the dossier decoder EXISTS and is tested (live-document-dossier.test.ts). Do NOT write a second one — a parallel decoder for a read the browser already decodes is exactly the duplication this board keeps paying for. So the row is: ONE new decoder (gate-1) + ONE new screen (contract dossier) + WIRING an existing decoder/component into v2 (PRD dossier). QA should grade DoD 3's dossier half as satisfied by reuse, with the test being that v2 renders it — not that a new decoder exists.
